hints.title: Describe all translations in one expression
hints.body: A horizontal translation changes the input of the cubic; a vertical translation adds a constant to its output. Write a formula with one parameter for each shift.
hints.recap: Combining several translations still gives one horizontal shift and one vertical shift.
hints.pitfall: A translation does not stretch the graph.
hints.pause: Write the general translated form of the basic cubic.

recall.reminder: A horizontal shift replaces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math>; a vertical shift adds a constant.

hints.title: Compare the linked coefficients
hints.body: Expand (x−a)3+b. Record how its coefficients of x3, x2, and x depend on the horizontal shift.
hints.recap: The horizontal shift controls more than one coefficient, so they cannot be chosen independently.
hints.pitfall: The vertical shift only changes the constant term.
hints.pause: Write the coefficient conditions that every translated cubic must satisfy.

recall.reminder: The binomial expansion gives the coefficients of a cube without choosing sample inputs.

hints.title: Test each proposed polynomial
hints.body: For each expression, first check the leading coefficient. If it is compatible, use the quadratic coefficient to determine the horizontal shift and then check the linear coefficient.
hints.recap: A consistent horizontal shift must explain both nonconstant lower coefficients.
hints.pitfall: A suitable constant term cannot repair a mismatch in a nonconstant coefficient.
hints.pause: Classify all three expressions, and for each surviving one find a vertical shift that completes the match.

recall.reminder: Graph translations impose a precise algebraic form, which can be checked coefficient by coefficient.

solution:
Any sequence of horizontal and vertical translations produces y=(x−a)3+b=x3−3ax2+3a2x−a3+b. Its leading coefficient remains 1.

For I, the coefficient of x2 forces a=1, which would give an x-coefficient of 3, not 9. So I is impossible. For II, a=3 gives the required coefficients −9 and 27; choosing b=24 also gives its constant −3.

III has leading coefficient 27, so it cannot be obtained by translations alone. Only II works. Answer C.
